newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany to let easterners buy their village.
newsitem.headline: Germany to let easterners buy their village.

text.p: Residents of this eastern German village celebrated on Friday after authorities who have been trying to sell the community to a single buyer for six years agreed to let individuals buy their own homes instead.
Liebenberg, 60 km (40 miles) north of Berline and site of a gothic castle, a stone church and about 50 houses, was to have been be sold in one block by the state agency BvS.

The BvS, and its predecessor the Treuhand, were charged with disposing of enterprises and property owned by former communist East Germany and it had been searching for a wealthy investor to take over Liebenberg which, like many villages in the east, had lapsed into a dire state of disrepair.
The villagers met in a local pub earlier this week and decided to launch a collective bid. That effort failed but they now at least will be able to buy their own homes.
Many years of efforts to sell Liebenberg to the state of Brandenburg collapsed earlier this year because the cost of renovations to homes, roads and other infrastructure was deemed to be prohibitive.
